newsitem.title: USA: Capline crude pipeline system unaffected by storm.
newsitem.headline: Capline crude pipeline system unaffected by storm.

text.p: Capline pipeline crude gathering points in St. James, Louisiana were not affected by Hurricane Danny on Friday, company sources at operator Shell Oil Co said Friday.
"Everything is running normal. The storm did not come close to St. James," said a Shell official said.
Capline is the major crude pipeline artery feeding the Midwest to Patoka, Illinois terminal from St. James with a capacity of 1.1-1.2 million barrels per day.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James grade differentials had run higher from the beginning of the week, partly on worries of damage from Hurricane Danny as the storm developed from a depression to a tropical storm and then Hurricane.
LLS barrels topped out at around 32-35 cents over the August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark price on Wednesday, but slipped back to premiums from 22-25 cents on Friday, crude traders said.
Danny was last reported heading northeast toward Mobile Bay, Alabama at about 5 miles (8 km) per hour, with sustained winds of 75 miles per hour (120 kmph).
Oil producers in the Gulf have begun scheduling restarts at platforms and other facilities as the storm passes by the U.S. oil refining and offshore production belt.
